content.text:
Dedicated workers in Chromium now get the context's locale. I couldn't build or run anything, so this is untested.

The change is in `packages/playwright-core/src/server/chromium/crPage.ts`, in the code that attaches to a new worker. If the context has a `userAgent` or `locale`, it now sends `Emulation.setUserAgentOverride` to the worker's session. The call carries the user agent, `acceptLanguage` set to the locale, and the user agent metadata. It goes out just before `Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger`, so the override should be in place before the worker script starts running. This is the same override the service worker code already sends.

That should fix both the `Accept-Language` header on requests made from inside the worker and `navigator.languages` in the worker.
